utterances.text: But that can be established in such a simple way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But that's what this is -- I mean, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, apparently I understood what you're aiming at. So you have achieved your goal, isn't it, that the matter is far more complex. At the same time, whether issues like arrest resolve the whole matter, whether law enforcement is purely a matter of arrest or administrative matters, there are a lot of instruments in law, as you may know, to enforce the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand where we are at this moment, what -- apparently I've understood part of the point you wished to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aiming at Mr. Theunens' conclusion that the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia pursuant to Article 118 had duties which they failed to enforce. I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm hopefully cross-examining to show Mr. Theunens actually doesn't understand what enforcement or regulation the Serbian MUP had, and that's, in our submission, a condition precedent for the conclusion that he's reached. If he doesn't understand the duties and the enforcement powers that the Serbian MUP had, then they cannot say that they failed to abide by them. That's the point. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless you take it a very -- I would say a very global level, that state organs have a general duty to -- to abide by the law and to do whatever is within their competence apart from what that is. And then we'll further have to look at that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Apart from what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in order to -- in order to ensure law enforcement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. And apart of what's within their competence, and this is what I submit Mr. Theunens hasn't analysed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the simple question is: Mr. Theunens, have you specifically looked into competencies as far as arrests are concerned, administrative enforcement? Apparently you have not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't looked at these detailed competencies but the conclusion is based on the fact that I haven't seen any document that any of the by then well-known paramilitaries or volunteers was arrested on the basis of Article 118. The only legal action that took place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from whether 118 is an article which would provide for a proper basis for arrest or whether you would have to rely on other legislation, such as the legislation on weapons and armament, because this law seems not to be very prominent in providing -- providing definitions of offences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. So -- but -- but to continue, for example the volunteers of the Radical Party, it is only after -- I mean on the basis of the material I have reviewed, it's only after there is a political fallout between Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Seselj that the state -- the competent state authorities in the Republic of Serbia, including the MUP, the police, arrest volunteers, I mean, senior volunteers who were affiliated to the SRS and they're all arrested on the basis of violation of the law -- of the legislation in relation to possession of arms. Article 118 never appears even if, in my conclusion, the possession of arms is directly related to activities they were conducting in violation of Article 118.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Let's then -- if I careful listen to you is the following, that where those who might have violated Article 118 most likely would have committed offences again the law on arms and ammunition as well, it comes as a surprise that it was so -- such a small number of arrests, which, although based on the Law of Arms and Ammunition, would be linked to activities you would consider to be relevant in the context of Article 118. That's apparently what your reasoning is without going into any further details as to the exact competencies of those who were, as you say, supposed to act or those who really acted. Mr. Jordash, I'm trying to understand what we're doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, you'll concede that that what Mr. -- what His Honour Judge Orie just said doesn't appear in your report. You don't quote from the relevant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear that the specifics on police investigations or prosecutions do not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They're not in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They're not in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry to step in. We're discussing one article. There are many other things that are referenced in the report and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not saying that there is not, but I'm trying to understand what Mr. Jordash apparently wants to elicit from this witness. And it's relatively simple. If you have a -- would have asked in the beginning apart from whether 100 -- Article 118 creates a proper basis for arrest where we see that arrests are usually done on other basis, have you specifically paid attention to these competencies, and do you not consider to form a final opinion on what should have done also in this respect, that you would have to need -- that you needed to attention to that as well. And then I think that Mr. Theunens would have easily said yes. I'm not quite sure, Mr. Theunens, but that's what I understand from your -- from the answers to some of my questions, and then we can move on. Which means that a certain element, a certain aspect is not dealt with in substance in drawing the conclusions. Now, whether what Mr. Theunens did deal with sufficiently support his conclusions is, of course, then another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I thought that's what I was aiming at but if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, apparently I -- if I understand you well, I have understood more or less what you were about to continue to ask Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what I'm trying to tell you is that why not get to the core of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Because I'm trying to highlight to Your Honours that the complexity of the situation, because we will in due course or we may in due course call evidence to establish in front of Your Honours what the competencies of the Serbian MUP were and to deal with the aspects of Mr. Theunens' analysis which we say he should have engaged in and failed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. He didn't -- he didn't pay attention to those specific aspects. That's the most important thing we've established now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, I -- as I said, for me this -- the -- the reply by Stojicic is an example. It shows that the Ministry of the Interior can arrest people for illegal possession of weapons. I think from the contents of my report it can be concluded that the groups you're talking about were in the possession of weapons and that these weapons were acquired in or via Serbia. And based on the fact that I've only see a document here for the arrest of Bokan and then -- but these documents are not included in this report, but arrests for volunteers of -- of Mr. Seselj's party, whereby these arrests only took place after there was a political conflict with Mr. Milosevic, I concluded from that that the legislation was selectively applied --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the report in fact says that Tode Vojvodic, his answer to a question indicates that the Serbian authorities in general and the Ministry of Interior in particular selectively enforced. Now you're adding to your report. That's the point. That's not what your report says at page 93. Anyway, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's coherent, but I haven't included the information on the SRS volunteers in my report, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's have a --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you have the Seselj report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's have a look -- well, we'll come to that shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't have the Seselj report, Mr. Theunens. You should be aware of that. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just putting on the record that I believe his opinion is that he -- that the article implies and I believe it's talked about on different context. I just -- Mr. Jordash is quoting to it, and I just wanted to make sure the opinion is on the record correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Jordash, please proceed, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It doesn't say "implies." It says "indicates."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the next break you are invited to sit together and to see whether it says "implies" or "indicates," and if there's any ongoing disagreement, the Chamber will be glad to further pay attention to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You only rely in your report on 118 as the sole criminal piece of legislation, don't you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not specifically. I mean, I -- I -- I use 118 to show that the Serbian authorities did not act against the establishment of -- of political party based volunteer groups as well as other groups which are not foreseen by -- by the legislation but, by analysing the documentation, proved to be controlled by or linked otherwise to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, even if these groups were not initially foreseen in the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you for the answer. Is there a power of arrest in 118?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. Is there a power of arrest in that particular piece of legislation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which particular piece of legislation?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The Law on Defence.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to look at it. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting it to you there isn't. You don't know.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's have a look at footnote 259, which is P1057.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please could we have that on e-court. You will have to forgive me, I don't have the e-court number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is P1057.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Oh. I beg your pardon. I'll come back to this. Could I just have a moment, please. Could -- could we have footnote 258, which is P1057, or is that the same one? I beg your pardon. Sorry, Your Honours. Let's move on. I'll come back to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to have a look instead at P1054, just moving back to page 92 of your report. Footnote 255 and 256, where you use this document to establish in your mind the notice that the Ministry of the Interior had concerning --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- private armed volunteer groups. If we look at page 1, we have a discussion in a response to Seselj's comments. And if we move down below, the answer to Seselj is the part I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior issues the following response with reference to 118, reiterating what it says, and then saying: "It's becoming more and more obvious --"

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you? Just the -- because I want to correct my previous answer. I said that Article 118 -- I agreed with you that you said -- you suggested it didn't have any implications to arrest, and I was just referring to the actual text as it is in the Law of Defence. But in this letter, actually, it is said that people can be in prison for 60 days now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's different to a power of arrest. That's a power of -- that's a punishment rather than a power of arrest, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, but in my nonlegal mind I assumed that imprisonment includes -- assumes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's get rid of this. If you want to imprison someone, if he reports voluntarily you don't have to arrest him. If you are talking about pre-trial arrest or arrest in the context of an investigation -- let's -- what you say, it's an offence, and let's leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because if it's not an offence, there should be no penalty.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page to have a look at the remaining answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we go back again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What was the significance you gave this -- this answer, that this informed the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. In Roman II on page 92, I drew the conclusion that this reply explicitly -- or shows that the Serbian Ministry of Interior explicitly recognised that it was aware of the existence of armed volunteer formations. Then I quote from the text, it is becoming more and so on until the end of the paragraph with carried out. I also quote the paragraph where it's stated that the Serbian -- the MUP of the Republic of Serbia is carrying out its duties. Maybe that's on the next page. Yes. I think on the fifth line, and I ended -- I mean that's on the top -- the bottom of page 92, part one, that the reply does not indicate which specific measures the MUP Serbia is taking.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you can see there that the ministry is saying that it's carrying out its duties in accordance with the Law on Defence. It is co-operating with the state authorities and is taking measures with an aim of preventing any activities of illegal armed groups on the territory of the republic. And it then states the operational work which is focused on illegal possession of arms, military training that is violating Articles 99 and 103 of the Law on Defence, and all other forms of paramilitary activities disturbing the public order. In that respect, MUP has filed 13 criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the document states, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. So it did give some detail about what the Serbian MUP was doing.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. You can discuss -- one can debate some detail or more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. Well let's go to P1048, please, which is at page 95 of your report, footnote 264. And you rely upon this report to show the -- to show the involvement of the Ministry of the Interior and the arming of volunteers and paramilitaries. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if we look at the text of the report, at page 1 we can see some detail in the second paragraph there. Four or five lines down. In addition, they are establishing arming and training party-related paramilitary groups. Some individuals are trying to get permission from their members and supporters to be trained at VJ barracks. Making preparations for attacks against military installations and operations to topple the legal authorities. Discouraging men liable for military service from responding to summons from military organs. And encouraging members of peacetime and reserve formations to operate VJ units from the party's positions. And attempting it get their own positions and support within the VJ. Was it known at that point that these political parties were organising groups and their aim was ultimately to topple the Serbian government? Is that something which was common to these opposition parties and their activities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were political parties who were organising armed groups. Now, it's not clear from the outset that they want to topple the Serbian government. It may be that some groups developed that goal, because obviously most of them were of nationalistic orientation and were suspicious of the Serbian authorities, but that's what I tried to explain and I try to be brief. Earlier that my conclusion is that somebody like Vojislav Seselj, for example, relied on the -- call it tacit authorisation of the Serbian authorities and his relationship with Slobodan Milosevic, his good relation with Slobodan Milosevic, in order to organise and so on the -- his groups, and that only when there was a political fallout between two in November 1993, that legal steps were put against his volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to -- you do accept then that many of these groups did want to topple the Serbian government?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends at which moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, in 1991, which ones do you think -- did you conclude wanted to topple the Serbian government?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't -- in my analysis I haven't addressed that specific aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's have a look at page 2 of this exhibit. You can see there at the top of the page the party -- perhaps we -- discussing the SPO. Who are the SPO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Renewal Movement of Vuk Draskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it says there at the top this party reportedly has detachments formed on paper all over Serbia which it plans to activate at a given moment to try to topple the legal authorities. Would you accept that that was the case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document states, but again when I would analyse that specific issue, I would also look for -- for other documents, from all documents, as I've done throughout my report for the topics I have discussed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You haven't put that in your report, have you, that this group wanted to at some point topple the legal authorities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I believed it was outside the scope of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move down the page to the third paragraph. The command of the Hajduk Veljko Detachment also has several platoons and assault groups of the Serbian Volunteer Guard subordinated to it which were formed in some of the bigger towns in south-eastern Serbia - there's the list of towns - and have the task of engaging in the forcible occupation of important military installations, MUP installations, and infrastructure, and prompting their members and supporters to engage in widespread armed insurrection at a given point -- moment in order to seize power. Isn't that something that was within your knowledge, Mr. Theunens, that this kind of activity was what the Serbian government was facing around this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were for sure groups that wanted to topple -- I mean, topple or act against the government because they were of very nationalistic orientation, but my focus in the report was on groups of parties that enjoyed good relations with the government. And there is, for example, in the document a reference to the paramilitary groups organised by the SRS --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you didn't consider in your report the groups that didn't enjoy good relations with the government?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because that was outside the scope of my report. And I mean, just to be complete, I -- I -- of course I conducted searches on the names of these groups but I couldn't really identify precise information on -- on their involvement in -- in issues that were of interest for this report. I know that the Serbian Renewal Movement -- I mean the Srpska Garda of the Serbian Renewal Movement were involved in operations in Gospic in 1991, but that was not within the scope of my report, these specific operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have a look, please, at 2 -- footnote 261, page 93 of your report. P1059. This is what you rely upon to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The document's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, not to be shown to the public. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is what you used to rely upon to show that the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia collected information on the activities of at least one volunteer group; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's footnote --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, it's 1058. P1058.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's footnote 260. Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if we could have a look at it, if we could, please. This is -- what is this, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an information, a report on the situation in Western Slavonia, i.e., in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. And it's a report which was sent, is this right, from the SSNO to the state security?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the heading clearly states SDB State Security of -- I mean, the Republic of Serbia, so the MUP. So it's -- it's -- according to what I see, it has been compiled by the SDB of the MUP Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: My mistake. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm going to have to come back to that actually. I do apologise, Your Honour. I tabulated things wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But of interest is that the SDB compiles a report about the situation in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's have a look, please, at P1059. Footnote 261, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it's what you rely upon to show further awareness by the Serbian MUP of information that the UB had collected on the alleged involvement of paramilitary and volunteer formations in the commission of crimes against the civilians in the RSK, including the identity of the alleged perpetrators. Now, this is what you would say is a report sent to the Serbian MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean I only see the cover page where it says SSNO, but then it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But looking at your -- your report at page 93, I think that you say the document, is this right, the document entitled "Analysis."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but we would have to go --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the ERN I put for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Information on the crimes against civilians.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Footnote 261 consists of a document that is sent by the -- the security administration, i.e., the SFRY Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sent to --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm sorry for the confusion. What I tried to do, I compared two different documents. I compared a document compiled by the state security of the Republic of Serbia. I think that was the previous document we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This was an information sent to the Serbian MUP and then there is a response document by the state security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, that's not how I described it in my report. Maybe, I don't know, during the break if I could look at the hard copies, I could check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Look at the clock, Mr. Jordash. That might even be a good suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it would and I can get my papers in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break and we resume at ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jordash. No, before I ask you to do that, Mr. Weber, I earlier asked you for information about the history of the scheduling of Witness 26. Of course, in the context it should have been understood as asking for the history of Witness JF-52.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's how I understood it, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go back to page 93 of chapter 1, Mr. Theunens. I want to have a look at two documents you detail there at (C), and you note, in relation to these two documents, that what you took from them was that the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia was aware of the information that UB had collected on the alleged involvement of Serbian paramilitary and volunteer formations in the commission of crimes against civilians in the RSK, including the identity of the alleged perpetrators. Was there nothing else you took from those documents of significance to the issues worth considering?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I addressed -- I used these documents in other sections of my report, but basically just a small correction. It's one document, P1060. That is a document compiled by the state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah, but the first document is P1059, which is the UB report, no?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And then there's P --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And P1060 is the state security document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is the response --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- of the state security. Let's have a look briefly at P1059, and what this is is a report, an information report. Is it a report to the -- sent from the SSNO to the Belgrade DB, department -- state security department?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what is on screen I can see that it's indeed a document from the SSNO, but I'm not sure where the addressee -- I can't see the addressee on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, if you look at your report, and we'll come to that in a minute, but it says which was compiled in response to a similar report by the UB.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. Or you're saying it may not have got -- it may not have been sent from the SSNO to the Belgrade DB?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. What I'm trying to say is that we should actually look at P1060, which the state security document, because that should then show -- could mention that it's compiled in response to the UB document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It does, and we'll get to that. It does.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So if you just take that one trust from me for the moment and then --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So let's look at 1059 and let's look at page 2, please. And its entitled, as you can see, "Information on the crimes against civilians." And then, I don't want to go through all of the document, but the document lists at page 2, crimes by -- or suspected crimes by the Valjevo TO Detachment with approximately ten members of the Dusan Silni Detachment.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And we can see page 3, and 3 of the B/C/S as well, further details there of the crimes alleged. And then if we go further down the page you can see that the persons -- or the institutions it was sent to.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You only quote, I think, very few -- I think it may be only this report from the SSNO to the Belgrade DB. Is that -- am I correct that it -- that you haven't come across many of these documents from the SSNO to the Belgrade DB?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. I mean, this is one of the few which explicitly indicates, and also on the first page, that the information is passed to the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There is no obligation on the SSNO to send information to the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the regulations that apply to that, but I would assume -- again it's my interpretation of the regulations that the SSNO UB, the security administration, would share information with the Ministry of the Interior if they're obliged by law, i.e., to ensure that the proper law enforcement measures are implemented or if there is an operational need to share the information. But again that's just my interpretation. I cannot refer to a specific regulation or legislation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. But --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe if we go back to page 1 because I saw a reference to Ministry of the Interior in the middle. Maybe that explains why it was sent to the Ministry of the Interior. It's in the middle of the page more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah. "However, while carrying out the basic tasks as the priority under the condition of combat activities and the nonexistence of the legally enforceable jurisdiction, as well as the fact that the purpose of the -- the perpetrators of these crimes would most often desert the unit immediately in an organised manner or on a self-initiative, the committed crimes were generally only registered and only partially documented. All information was immediately passed on to the local organs of government, the organs of internal affairs of the Republic of Serbia," and so on.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's what I tried to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What did you try to say, sorry?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, as I explained earlier, that the SSNO -- or the UB of the SSNO forwarded the information because there was an operational requirement or in order to ensure that the proper law enforcement measures were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. So are you not surprised that you haven't come across more of these types of documents in your time with the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, because as you know, most of the documents I -- I had were documents that the 1st Military District sent to the SSNO. This is one of the few documents we had at the time when I compiled my report that is compiled at the level of the SSNO.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I can assure you that such documents were requested at the time, not specifically -- not only for this case but for many other cases before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. If we go -- thank you. If we go to -- are we on page 3? Can we go it page 3, because there's a report there of an incident in the Lovas village.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And are you familiar with who the perpetrators were and whether there was a follow-up by the SSNO in terms of these suspected crimes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I think the perpetrators belong to the Dusan Silni group. When -- I say "I think" because I remember there is the letter or the report by Lieutenant-Colonel Eremija, who was the officer responsible for morale in the Proletarian Guards Motorised Division, i.e., the unit that covered the area of Lovas at the time, and I think this report dates from fall 1991, in which this crime -- sorry, in which this crime or this alleged crime and the alleged perpetrators are described. I am not familiar with the follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at page 4, please. You see there noted halfway down the page the authorised official from the military post Novi Sad -- 4323 Novi Sad submits a criminal report against Strigic, Slobodan, to the military proud, the VP 282 Belgrade. Strigic, as we can see further up the page, was a member of special purpose unit of the Beli Manastir SUP and yet he was prosecuted by the military police. Why would that be?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- I mean, we would have to go through the whole document because maybe he was somebody with -- I mean, I'm just -- maybe he was somebody with military speculation -- a military obligation, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What do you mean military obligation? In which circumstances would the military police jurisdiction kick in, if I can put that way?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was -- for sure if he was a member of a military unit at the time of when the crimes were committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Are you surprised that such a report dated May 1992 emanating from the SSNO doesn't include such things as Arkan and his conduct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a question of surprise. This is a document about, I think -- I would have to go through the whole document again, but I believe it deals with specific crimes, and more specifically the one in Lovas.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, but it's dealing with -- if we can go to page 2. It's dealing with issues which relate largely to SBWS; is that correct? And quite -- and also probably Srpska Krajina generally. You see at the top of page 2. Wouldn't you have expected a report at this level to have included Arkan within it at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, because we don't know -- I would assume that this is not the only report. There may be also reports on Arkan. We know that the 1st Military District compiled, and actually at a much earlier stage, we looked at them in fall 1991, quite a substantial number of reports on Arkan. They were sent to the SSNO. I -- since I don't have the documents from the security administration of the SSNO, I don't know what the SSNO did with the reports it received from subordinate security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And are you surprised -- that same question in relation to Ovcara, the massacre in Ovcara by certain members of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the trial judgement and the appeals judgement state that the executions were committed by members of volunteer groups who were operating under the command of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah, but no mention in this report, but that's to you not a surprise?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, there maybe another report on -- on Ovcara. Ovcara is a very complex issue. If you want, we can go into detail, but I'm not sure whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, I don't think that is necessary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I mean this is not an exclusive report. If we could -- if we would establish this is the only report the SSNO prepared, then indeed there maybe reason for surprise and then we would look into why only one report. But I cannot establish whether there were more reports, and I cannot establish whether this is the only report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to P1060, the response by the DB to this report. And it's dealt with in the same -- sorry, across the page 94 in your report. Footnote 262.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And to answer your question from the beginning why -- where you said that why do you only -- or why did you deal with that document in such a brief manner, I just used the document for the section notice of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah. But you didn't, and this is what I find significant, and I would suggest it is significant in relation to your methodology. You don't include the response by the DB and what its response was, which I suggest is -- well, is an interesting response given your thesis. Page 1, analysis -- so this is a state security department sent to Belgrade, 27th of May, 1992, responding to the SSNO's number 236, dated the 26th of May, 1992. And if we go from page 1 to page 2, you'll see that -- and I suggest if you read this, you'll see that the DB take -- took its responsibilities fairly seriously and carefully, I suggest, analysed its own jurisdiction. We see, for example, on page 2, paragraph 1 and I'll just read part of it: "The responsibility for the sufferings of the civilians, first and foremost, lies with Lieutenant-Colonel Miodrag Dimitrijevic and the reserve commanding officers, Peric Darko and Vlajkovic Radovan, both from Valjevo." And then it gives a description. And then in brackets it says: "We think that the military prosecutor would have authority for the possible criminal procedure against these persons."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And then down the page to paragraph 2, noting in response to the crimes against women, a criminal report has been filed with the authorised military prosecutor's office and the investigation is ongoing. And same with 3. And doesn't this response by the DB indicate exactly what I've just said, that this was the DB responding in a way which you suggest the Serbian MUP didn't respond, which was to take its responsibilities seriously? Did you not think that was worth putting in the report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- my view on paragraph 1 or the part that you read out simply shows that the DB confirms the existing legislation to the military, i.e., that members of the armed forces who have allegedly committed crimes shall be investigated and -- or shall face military jurisdiction. It would be useful if I could compare the two documents then to see whether if the UB document also identified civilians, for example, among the volunteers of Dusan Silni, what the recommendations of the DB in their regard was. Or maybe you can do that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I can, for example -- sorry, what are you saying is the jurisdiction, then, of the DB in this situation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not so much saying what the jurisdiction is. I'm trying to answer to your question in -- if you want, I can repeat it. Military regulations are very clear that military personnel who have allegedly commit -- or who are suspected of having committed a crime, they shall face military justice system. I mean, military justice. My question was to see whether in the UB report civilians are identified or people, not members of the armed forces, like, for example, Dusan Silni group, whether any reference is made to them in the -- in this -- in this DB report here and see what the recommendations or the action undertaken by the DB or the -- is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's have a look at page 4. Well, yes. Let's go to page 1, first of all, to see what the analysis, the first analysis says. The DB is saying of the information received "with accompanying documentation on the possibility of taking to court the persons who committed crimes against the civilians." So this document appears to be, don't you agree, an response by the DB looking into the possibility of its own jurisdiction being operative?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but -- I'm sorry if I repeat it again, but the military -- I mean the regulations on -- the 1977 regulation on military prosecutor and military courts do not make any references to the state security in relation to the enforcement of justice against members of the armed forces. So what I'm trying to say is that the UB has sent this document with a particular motive to the DB, and one possible motive could be that the UB, in addition to military suspects or alleged perpetrators, has also identified civilian alleged perpetrators where these would not necessarily be put or be the subject of military justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's have a look at page 3, paragraph 7, and it says: "In the case of the killing of 16 civilians, most of them Croats, which took place on the night of the 6th and 7th November 1991, no evidence was submitted along. In the analysis of the information, it was said -- it is said that a group of approximately 20 volunteers led by Gogic Milan, aka Zuka, from Novi Sad, was engaged in that area, the village of Enton [phoen], SO Vukovar, besides the unit of the JA, SUP Serb SBWS carried out an investigation. Further authority lies with the SB JNA as written in the SUP which carried out the investigation in the SRDB Novi Sad." Isn't that the issue that you were addressing? Isn't that the DB saying, well, actually this may be a situation where we might have jurisdictio for the reasons that you've just given and we're going to look into it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah. And if we look over the page to page 4, number 9, with reference to the Zuca, the Vuckovic male, one of two brothers, I think.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you can see what reference there is that -- that he's a criminal from Belgrade, no note -- no reference there to him being part of a unit which doesn't seem to be information that the DB has, and then -- then consideration of what the DB could arrest him for. Isn't that again a similar point? In the absence of his stated connection to the JNA or TO, the DB then considers what it can do.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he was -- I assume you will come back to Vuckovic at a later stage when we discuss Zvornik but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- anyway that's in my report. But yeah, it states here that he was arrested -- oops. I touched the screen. But for illegal possession of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Didn't you think that this was significant, that of the very few reports that you received of the SSNO reporting to the Belgrade DB centre, and you get what I can suggest is a pretty careful response, it seems on the face of it, didn't you think that was important to mention in the report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that I could have put -- included this reference that he was arrested for the possession and carrying of firearms. I could have added that to the Bokan letter as an additional footnote, but otherwise, as I said earlier, I used this document solely for the purpose of notice, because we are -- I gave the answer already two times. I don't see -- I mean, now, looking at it again, anything significant that the Ministry of the Interior undertook except for reminding the military of what their duties were in relation to the enforcement of military justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. I'll leave the point there if you didn't find it significant. Let me move to Mr. Seselj, which you've returned to on many occasions during your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on e-court, please, 65 ter 1D1349, page 1D01-7542.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this is some of your comments, I think, on some issues of relevance here. Well, that's difficult to read. This is your testimony in the Seselj case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we go slightly up the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The -- you're discussing, as you can see there, the role of political -- certain political parties in the establishment of paramilitary formations, and your response to a question, were these formations based on material that you have reviewed supported by the Republic of Serbia. And you say: "Well, overall, as an overall comment one would say that they were at least allowed to exist. There are indications that some groups were the subject of investigation or even that they were prevented from continuing to exist, and I refer, I think, to the Serbian Volunteer Guard in specific references."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you just elaborate on that is answer in the Seselj case, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be an error. I must have meant the Serbian Guard so I don't -- I mean, I don't check transcripts. Okay, I should check them when I'm testifying but -- the Serbian Volunteer Guard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the transcript is the exclusive responsibility -- it's good that if any mistake was made that it is corrected, but you have no duty to verify the transcript when testifying. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I must have meant the Serbian Guard, Srpska Guard of Vuk Draskovic, because we've touched upon that a few times. There, as far as I remember, action was undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When were they prevented from continuing to exist, and by whom?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly. What I recall is that they were involved in Gospic, I believe in the summer or fall 1991. And then you still saw some kind of open-source reporting on alleged activities, but including references also in security organ reports, but I don't -- I cannot say exactly when -- or when they were disbanded. I have a recollection that they were disband -- I mean that they were -- sorry, not just disbanded out of their own volition but action was undertaken. But I have no exact recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the Serbian -- I mean Serbian government. I mean the Serb -- the competent Serb authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And who would they be?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would involve the -- I mean the Ministry of the Interior, maybe the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You didn't think that important to put in your report in this case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the issue. I mean, what I said there in Seselj is -- is based on my general knowledge. As you see in this report for -- except for the conclusions I draw on the facts, for each fact there is a reference. Now, obviously I cannot find -- I don't have reference for each and every thing I remember about the conflict in the former Yugoslavia, and this is one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But you were analysing the responsibilities of the MUP and their tacit authorisation of opposition paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How significant were the Serbian Guard in terms of these types of groups?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's always difficult to -- to -- to mention -- to judge the significance, but at least based on my research they were -- as I mentioned they were involved in one area, in Gospic, so in the Krajina, and other areas I found some general references in -- in documents of the 1st Military Districts but nothing at the level of the groups I have discussed in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I mean, you make mention through -- throughout your report of the Serbian Guard, don't you, in this case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can remind me where? I mean probably I mentioned them at least once or twice but not as often as -- as Arkan or Dragan or volunteers belonging to the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Well, let's leave the point there. Let's -- you do make the point there in the next line about focusing in the Seselj case on this Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the conclusion that there was co-operation with the Ministry of Defence and/or the Ministry of Interior in order to organise, equip, arm, and dispatch these units, as well as co-operation with the JNA. Is there any reason you said "and/or" in that case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, grammatically speaking, "and" would have been sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to 65 ter, please, on the e-court, 1D1349. 1D134G -- 9, sorry. 1D1349. And page, first of all, 1D01-7667.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this is where you deal with, I think, Seselj's relationship with Slobodan Milosevic at some point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we just -- if we go down the page, please. Could we go back up a little. And you say, I think -- keep going, please. "THE WITNESS: This is public knowledge, referring to number 3 on the list. I'm sorry if this -- I don't -- if you aren't able to locate this in context, then we can come back to it, Mr. Theunens. But Mr. -- what is said there is Mr. Seselj suspected that person of having, yeah, particular links, i.e., that he was collecting information for the state security of the Republic of Serbia. Is this a man called Petkovic? And I remember that was a time when this person was kicked out of the War Staff, a press conference whereby this person more or less had to make a confession about his ties with the state security of the Republic of Serbia. Mr. Seselj sitting on his left or his right side."

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Does this trigger your memory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the -- the chief of the SRS War Staff. At the time I don't recall his exact name but I can find --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We'll come back to it anyway. But it was somebody kicked out of -- a prominent person in the --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of the SRS War Staff during the relevant time period, i.e., from, I think, end of 1991, because he's -- I think his predecessor was Zoran Rankovic and he took over from Rankovic. But I can find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah. No, we'll come to that. I think --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's Petkovic, I think.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but in the first name I'm not hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But he was kicked out when?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in the latter half of 1993, but I can be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: He was kicked out for what in particular, do you know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the open-source information states that Vojislav Seselj was suspicious that the co-operation he had with the Serbian government Ministry of Defence as well as the Ministry of the Interior went beyond what I would call advancing the goals of the War Staff, but that actually, according to Mr. Seselj, this person was, yeah, collecting information on the activities of the War Staff and the SRS for the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go down the page a bit please. Judge Antonetti then asks you -- we're keeping the court staff busy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI ASKS YOU
utterances.text: "This event indicates that in the Republic of Serbia there were power struggles or between the political parties, the MUP and the Ministry of the Interior, there was a struggle to exert influence; is that right? Can you confirm this?" And you say: "... and more specifically that the competent services, i.e., the State Security Service, was aware that certain political parties were organising, I mean recruiting, organising, dispatching volunteers, and also involved in arming them, and from that legal point of view it made sense to keep an eye on them, even though it seems that it took some time before there was any --" can we go over the page, please -- "before there was any action against these activities." And you say: "This is not dealt with in my report but I remember that it's only after a political conflict arises between Mr. Seselj and Mr. Milosevic sometime in October 19 -- November 1993 that the competent authorities in Serbia start with the arrest of volunteers, and they're all arrested -- or most of them are arrested on the ground of illegal possession of firearms and they're released quite soon." So you're there making a clear distinction, it seems, between what the state security was doing, which was keeping them under surveillance, and then the competent authorities making the arrests somewhat later in the day. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the state -- I mean the competent authorities can include the state security. I have -- as I said today, I have not analysed the detailed tasks or competence of the state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we go to page 1D01-7668 -- oh, we've just had a look at that. Okay. Can we go then to 65 ter 1D1349, the same one, page number 1D01-8164.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I mean, you've said on a number of occasions today, I think, that Seselj was, I think this is right, allowed to -- by the -- by the competent authorities in Serbia to arm himself; is that right? If not today, this is something you've said before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and, I mean, we have the testimony in Seselj and I have also included some of these -- some of the statements Mr. Seselj made at the time in my report. He stated that he had -- he collaborated with the Ministry of Defence as well as with the Ministry of Interior Republic of Serbia, and when we talk about specific operations, and the one I recall now is the -- are the operations in Eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina early 1993. There is extensive publications by the SRS as well as statements by Mr. Seselj that these operations were conducted in direct co-ordination with Mr. Frenki Simatovic, i.e. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, we're going to come to some of that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But interesting that you don't preface these remarks with open source. When you implicate the Serbian MUP or the accused, you don't preface it with open source.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's open source, but I mean -- open source, I don't have any qualification in relation to it. Open source is just material that is available to the public. I think the first day I said that in traditional, call it intelligence work, it's generally stated that 80 perk cent of the information comes from open sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And of course there are certain caveats that may apply to open sources, but Mr. Seselj made a lot of public statements and, okay, they are obviously open source but I refer to them as Mr. Seselj's statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go back one page so we can get the context of what you're saying in the Seselj case. And you were asked that -- that's perfect. "How did volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party in the Serbian village of Slavonia from April to September 1991 obtain weapons? Where did they get their weapons from? Answer me that." And your answer was: "Your Honours, that's the question -- that question was already asked before the break, and I replied that they received the weapons from -- in the area, so from the local village defence. However, while reviewing my report during the break, I also found a statement by Mr. Soskocanin, who participated in the incident in Borovo Selo, who made a reference to the JNA. It's a very general reference, but anyway, that's included in my report." What precisely were you trying to say in that paragraph during the Seselj case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this deals with a very specific situation. It is the -- the incident in Borovo Selo on the 1st and the 2nd of May, 1991, and my testimony there is based on public statements and articles in SRS publications whereby the SRS describes in detail how its volunteers travel from Serbia to Borovo Selo, contact local Serb armed structures that are developing there, i.e., the local Serb TO that is being established. And according to these articles, weapons -- I cannot say all weapons, but weapons are provided by these local Serb TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. So they're travelling through Serbia to Borovo Selo and then obtaining their weapons when they arrive?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Now -- I mean it's not in the testimony, but if you want to be fully accurate, there's again open source information but I also would like to refer to P1048 when we deal about weapons of SRS volunteers. With open source information --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What does that say, that exhibit, sorry?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: P1048 states -- it's on page 94, part 1 of my report. It states under the heading "Paramilitary groups organised by the SRS." And then a large number of the people who have joined these formations are armed mostly with small arms from depots of the former JNA, MUP, and Serbian Ministry of Defence that were distributed in large numbers and so on and so on. What I was trying to say also is that the local Serb TO, on one hand, they could lay their hands on weapons that were there even if -- and again I don't want to be too detailed but the JNA had taken control over all these weapons. And that goes back to, I think, an order of May 1990. And in addition, weapons were distributed by the Ministry of Defence and, according to Seselj, also the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia to these local Serb defence structures, i.e., the local Serb TO that was established in parts of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you base that on that exhibit, do you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only on that exhibit. I mean, when I refer to the order, the Adzic order, it's in part 1 of the report. It's May 1990. It has to do with the Jedinstvo restructuring plan and the distribution of weapons by the Ministry of Defence. There's other documents in my report that refer to that and there's also open sources on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go further down the page, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You were asked -- it's put to you that they couldn't obtain the weapons from the local TO because the JNA took all the weapons from the TO. And you say you're aware of the order of May 1990 by General Adzic to relocate the weapons of the TOs of the republic and the autonomous provinces to JNA warehouses, but I understood that some of these weapons in the course of the conflict were redistributed to Serbs in various parts of Croatia. And you do then say later on down this page with reference to information that the JNA assisted together with the MUP and the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we go further down the page, please. To the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: To redistribute weapons to Serbs in various parts of Croatia. What did you mean by redistribute?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a result of the May 1990 order of General Adzic, the weapons of the Territorial Defence of the republics, I mean, should have been put in depots that were under JNA control. Contrary to the previous situation where the TO was in control of these depots. I didn't analyse that issue in detail but, okay, it's common knowledge that not all weapons were put under JNA control. Now, at the same time we also see that -- or later on, I'm sorry. Later on, in the course of 1991, there are examples of JNA units in control of TO weapons in areas with the Serb -- or significant Serb presence in Croatia distributing these weapons, or some of them, to the local Serbs as a part of the development of local Serb defence structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So were you saying there then that the MUP and the Ministry of Defence had collaborated to redistribute those weapons which were already in Croatia then? Is that what you were saying there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I'm trying to say is that there are different origins of these weapons. There are weapons that were already in Croatia and which -- and they belonged formally -- they are formerly to the Croatian TO, and then other weapons -- I mean, weapons were also provided by the Ministry of the Interior, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Redistributed by the -- so they're already in Croatia according to what you're saying. Isn't that fair?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think you're kind of mixing it up. I'm trying to explain what I meant by my testimony. I'm looking for the word "redistributed" now but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You can see it at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but then we --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Let's go back then.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What -- I mean what is -- what happened was that the weapons originated from -- I mean, there were different origins, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But there you're saying that the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia - and go over the page - in -- please --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In -- redistribute weapons to Serbs in various parts of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can correct "redistribute" there in the sense that I was told and I remember very well, for example, doing a suspect interview of Miodrag Jokic --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, are we going to hear about new evidence that you have picked up --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- which is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're asking for an explanation if the witness thinks that -- if there's anything that comes to his mind might assist him in explaining that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Miodrag Jokic, who has been minister of defence of the Republic of Serbia, he explained, without being very precise, that weapons held by factories, and that brings us back to the point you raised earlier of the role of state-owned factories in the defence system, I'm not sure whether it was in 1990 or even earlier, were gathered, because these were old weapons. It's the famous Thompsons and so on, weapons that were, I mean from Second World War. They were collected and I believe with -- I mean with the involvement of Ministry of Defence and/or the Ministry of the Interior, and then these weapons were redistributed to Serbs or distributed to Serbs in -- in Croatia. And this explains, for example, that -- I mean there's famous pictures of local Serbs in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem holding check-points with a Thompson style -- I mean, a Thompson World War II machine-gun. And to my recollection, that was not a weapon that was part of the inventory of the Republic of Croatia TO. And I see that in the testimony Mr. Seselj also gave an additional explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's go to that. I want to go further down the page because Seselj says to you: "Let's cut this short. I'll tell you what I know about this and you can confirm whether it's correct or not. These are weapons written off by the JNA set aside to be destroyed. General Dusan Pekic, one of the functionaries of the Association of Serbs from Croatia, using his private contacts and channels because he was a well-known famous commander from World War II, one of the most able generals the JNA ever had, and although he had been a partisan, I speak very highly of him, so he had good contacts. And using his private contacts with certain officers, he managed to obtain those weapons which had been earmarked for destruction. Am I correct in saying this? You mention Dusan Pekic in your report."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed it's correct. And I will just highlight we are not thinking again in exclusives. Pekic played an important role together with other members of the Association of Serbs in Croatia -- from Croatia to organise local Serb defence structures as did the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of the Interior, as I have explained in this particular report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. Let's go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I just want to correct Ministry of Defence and Ministry of the Interior to the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So Pekic played an ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are documents from the Association of Serbs in Croatia and they -- again I haven't analysed that here but I know from the Milosevic case they had also contacts with the Ministry of Defence. They would meet or they would seek contacts with General Simovic [Realtime transcript read in error "Simatovic"] and played a role and participate in the organisation of defence structures of Serbs in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to note on line -- page 90, line 18, it reflects Simatovic. I believe the witness said Simovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, it's Simovic, minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby corrected. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we go to the top of this page, please -- sorry, I can -- could we go three pages on, please, to 4334 in the right-hand corner. Three more pages. Sorry, I cannot count. And you were asked by

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: "Can you confirm or deny that the arms were given to volunteers through the channel of General Pekic who was able through his networks to send arms who seemingly were designed for destruction? Can you confirm Mr. Seselj's theory or not?" Can we go up the page, please. Mr. Theunens, you answer -- please keep going. "Your Honours, I confirm that thesis but it's not the only the channel. I'm aware that in -- I'm not sure if it was 1989 or 1990, that, for example, that in Serbia weapons at the civil defence and also weapons that were used or could be used in time of conflict or other condition when there was a requirement to do so, to protect factories and so on, were all confiscated or brought together. And I'm not sure anymore whether that was done by the Ministry of Defence or the Ministry of Interior." Do you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah it's the same I said today. I testified today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "Just to come back to Pekic. I think in any organised country, and the SFRY was certainly an organised country in 1990, you cannot just redistribute weapons through private channels. Procedures have to be followed, documents have to be established, and so on and so on. So the police most likely didn't have any Thompsons or M-84s or other old weapons in its equipment. But one cannot rule out that the police or the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of" - if we go over the page please - "Serbia played a road in organising the transit or redistribution of these weapons. That's what I was trying to say." Now, that is different to what you've been saying today, isn't it? One cannot rule out is very different to a positive assertion that they did.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I have, for example, in my report here P1048. I've mentioned it earlier. I'm not sure whether I had -- I mean, at the time I was testifying I remember that document, and my testimony is also a reply to quite aggressive - I mean, what I would qualify aggressive - questioning by Mr. Seselj -- yeah. Otherwise, I don't see a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, if you don't see a difference, that's fine. We leave it on the record as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Theunens, let's be -- if you cannot rule out something or if you positively establish something, I mean to say I can't see the difference. I think I would underestimate your intelligence if I would accept that for an answer. You know that there's a difference. Now, what your testimony today and what explains the difference. If you say, I was a bit intimidated at the time therefore I was overcautious, that's one explanation. Or if you'd say, Well, the questions by Mr. Seselj were such that I had to adapt slightly my too positive -- all possible explanations, but to say that you don't see the difference, that seems not to be something we'd like to accept at 5 minutes to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're fully right, Your Honours. I'm -- I'm trying to remember if I was aware of P1048 at the time or not, because P1048 for me is a quite strong document. And, of course, the whole discussion with Mr. Seselj is also that he was very vocal in the early 1990s and especially in particular after he broke with Mr. Seselj -- with Mr. Milosevic, and okay, once he was here in The Hague he came with different views.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's move on. 65 ter 1D1349, please, on e-court. Page 1D01-8147. If we go to the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So let's read your answer to -- let's go further up the page. Sorry. You were asked the question now -- so -- Mr. Seselj asks you this question: "Mr. Theunens, we're talking about up to September, up to the month of September, no a single volunteer of the Serbian Radical Party was in Western Slavonia. Isn't that right? So don't mix things up before September and after September, if you're able to do that. Are you able to do that? "So up until September, the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party were defending certain villages called in by the local Serb population to do so. Now, do you know that those volunteers crossed over into Slavonia, crossed the Danube or Srem, and they had to hide from the authorities in Serbia to do that?" Could we go up the page, please. "Your Honours, first of all, I would like comment on the fact -- on the claim made by Mr. Seselj that these volunteers had been called by the local Serb population to come to the area. I would like to refer you to English page 104 in page [sic] 2 of the report, where the activities of the Chetnik volunteer detachment that participated in the -- okay, the conflict in Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May has been discussed. And according to 65 ter number 320, that Chetnik volunteer detachment had been established following a decision by the Central Homeland Administration of the Serbian Chetnik Movement and then dispatched to Western Srem on the 2nd of April, 1991." Can we go up, please. "Now the circumstances of how these volunteers went from Serbia to Croatia. Indeed, articles of 'Velika Srbija' suggested the volunteers did not use one of the three bridges over the Danube but that they crossed --" Can we turn, please. "-- that they crossed the Danube by night using boats." You stand by that answer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of -- I mean the volunteers that participated in the Borovo Selo incident -- yeah, clash, yes, I haven't come across other information, so that's the best knowledge I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, you didn't say that in this case, did you, in your report or in your evidence that the Seselj men were having to cross surreptitiously because, for some reason, the Serbian authorities were preventing them crossing use the three bridges. Why didn't you say that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, I confirmed that -- but that based on the information in "Velika Srbija" they crossed the Danube using barges, and okay, this is the situation in May 1991. And you will see in my report, I mean the report in this case, that according to, for example, Branislav Vakic, he says that there is over time -- and Branislav Vakic was a senior SRS volunteer. Over time there was a change in his view in the attitude of the Serbian authorities in relation to politically oriented volunteers. And I can assure you, I mean, the SRS volunteers, again based on the information I have seen, who participated in the operations in Vukovar after September 1991, they were bus -- they were coming in by bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock. I heard your sigh. Isn't it that Shakespeare says "a thousand thousand sighs to save," but perhaps for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we'll continue tomorrow in the afternoon, quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom I. We adjourn until then unless you have some follow-up, Mr. --
